the soft-overlap contribution to form factors is dominated by Sudakov logarithms, which are resummed at leading order in the hard-scattering corrections, and that the hard-scattering contribution is also dominated by Sudakov effects, but these are not resummed at any order in the soft-overlap corrections.

the hard-scattering corrections to heavy-to-light currents and form factors at large energy transfer and large recoil have been computed to all orders in perturbation theory, that the leading-order results are in excellent agreement with numerical simulations, that the hard-scattered contributions are dominated by the soft-overlap contribution, and that the soft-overlap corrections are dominated by the leading-twist contribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the leading-power contribution to the form factors for semileptonic decays of heavy quarkonia.
the calculation of heavy-to-light transition form factors at large momentum transfer.
the calculation of heavy-to-light form factor at large recoil in the soft-collinear limit, and the resummation of the large logarithms arising in this limit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have now a complete understanding of the large recoil region in heavy-to-light form factor, including all the large logarithms.
the soft-overlap form factors are not affected by Sudakov logarithms, while the hard-scattering form factors are.

the resummation of large logarithms in the hard-scattering contribution to heavy-to-light semileptonic decays is well understood in SCET, and that this resummation is a crucial ingredient in the determination of the heavy-quark masses from experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to perform a resummed calculation of the hard-scatterings contributions to heavy-to-heavy form factors at large momentum transfer.
we have shown the resummation of the Sudakov double logarithms to all orders, and the resummation for the single logarithms up to two orders in SCET.
we have completed the leading-logarithm resummation for all heavy-to-light form factor in SCET.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hard-scattering corrections to form factors are dominated by Sudakov logarithms.

the hard-scattering contribution is not suppressed by a factor of 1/ m _{Q} compared to the soft-overlap contribution, but instead has a coefficient function that falls off as 1/ mQ ^{2}, so that its contribution is comparable to that of the soft-overlaps at large recoil.
the hard-scattering and soft-overlap contributions have a common large logarithmic structure, and that the resummation of logarithms in both cases is governed by a single anomalous dimension.
